0.0.n: Sets the scene in an earlier period of the speaker’s life.

0.2.n: A borrowed music-industry term referring to a large record company.

0.3.n: Marks the organization the speaker belonged to, with いる.

0.4.n: Past form of いる; here it describes belonging to a label.

0.5.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before です.

0.6.n: Makes the explanation polite; いた already supplies the past tense.

0.7.n: Links this background to what follows, gently suggesting a contrast.

1.0.n: そこ refers to the label, and で marks where the releases happened.

1.1.n: リリースする becomes リリースしていた to describe ongoing or repeated activity in the past.

1.2.n: Follows a verb phrase to identify the time during which something happened.

1.3.n: Marks 時 as the time when the speaker’s feelings changed.

2.0.n: Shows the speaker wanted a greater degree of freedom.

2.1.n: Combines with に to describe how the speaker wanted to release music.

2.2.n: Turns 自由 into a description of how an action is done.

2.3.n: Refers back to the speaker as the person who likes the songs.

2.4.n: Inside this description of 曲, の can replace が to mark who likes the songs.

2.5.n: Describes the speaker’s preference; Japanese treats 好き as an adjective, not a verb.

2.6.n: Connects 好き to the noun 曲 so it describes the songs.

2.7.n: Refers to musical pieces; Japanese does not require a plural ending.

2.8.n: Marks the songs as what the speaker wants to release.

2.9.n: The したい form of する expresses a desire to do the action.

2.10.n: Adds a gentle, inward-looking feeling to the speaker’s wish.

2.11.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思う.

2.12.n: Names the thought that began developing, with ようになる expressing the change.

2.13.n: In verb + ようになる, helps express a change into doing or experiencing something.

2.14.n: Links よう to なる, marking the new state the speaker came to experience.

2.15.n: て-form of なる; completes the change expression and connects it to the next event.

3.0.n: A conversational connector that moves the story forward, not a location particle here.

3.2.n: Connects the desire for freedom to the resulting decision.

3.3.n: Refers to the speaker; 自分の emphasizes personal ownership here.

3.4.n: Links 自分 to レーベル to show whose label it is.

3.5.n: A borrowed term for a company or brand that releases music.

3.6.n: Marks the label as what the speaker will establish.

3.7.n: Used for establishing an organization or project; the plain form comes before こと.

3.8.n: Turns 立ち上げる into an action that can be treated as the object of a decision.

3.9.n: Part of ことにする, the expression for deciding to do something.

3.10.n: Polite past form of する; with ことに, expresses a decision the speaker made.

0.lit: Previously, at a major record label I was, you see, but…
0.tip: いたんです adds a polite explanatory tone to the simple past statement いた.

1.lit: There, at the time I was releasing music…
1.tip: A verb phrase before 時 tells you when something happened.

2.lit: I came to think, I want to release songs I like more freely, and…
2.tip: 思うようになって describes a change: the speaker began to think or feel this way.

3.lit: So, because of that, I decided on starting up my own label.
3.tip: Verb + ことにしました means the speaker decided to do that action.
